$comment: Every distribution in this repository that declares a version nobody can
install, with the reason that state is acceptable. Measured by
`scripts/declared_publication_sweep.py`, guarded by
`tests/architecture/test_declared_publication.py`.
## Why this file exists at all
`test_module_version_sync.py` proves a module's three version surfaces
AGREE. It cannot prove the agreed version EXISTS. `dotmac-integration`
reads 0.1.0a2 on all three surfaces and the version-identity guard passes,
while the newest tag is dotmac-integration-v0.1.0a1 — internal consistency
and publication are different questions, and only the first one had a
guard. A consumer reading the repository, the changelog or
docs/MODULE_CATALOG.md and pinning ==0.1.0a2 gets a resolver error.
## What a row here does and does not mean
A row means the state is KNOWN and someone has said why. It is not
permission to leave it there, and it is emphatically not a reason to edit
the declared version down to match the index: that would make the
repository agree with the registry by discarding the work the number
describes, and the changelog entry for the unpublished version would then
belong to nothing.
The repair is not always a release, either. `dotmac-imports` was reported
as an anomaly BECAUSE it was release-allowlisted with no tag; the ruling
was that the allowlist row was the wrong half, and it was removed rather
than the module published. Two states this file must keep distinct:
* INTENDED — the distribution is meant to be unpublished right now.
The row records the decision so
the next reader does not undo it by dispatching a release.
* OUTSTANDING — a version is genuinely owed to consumers. The row
records evidence a decision still needs. Two worked examples have now
passed through and been removed on release: `dotmac-integration`
0.1.0a2 (released as a3) and `dotmac-kernel` 0.1.0a67. A row that
expires on its own release is the healthiest shape an entry here has.
Both are recorded the same way and neither is a pass. The reason text is
where the difference lives, which is why the guard requires a premise
rather than a label.
## Two directions, both failures
A distribution entering this state without a row fails — that is a version
silently promised to consumers. A row whose distribution has since been
published ALSO fails and must be removed in the same change as the release,
because a ledger that only grows stops describing anything (ADR-0018).
## The oracle is a git tag
The release workflows write a tag only after `verify-registry` has
installed the exact published version from the private index and registered
its manifest, so a tag is this repository's own assertion that a version is
installable — stronger than 'an upload succeeded'. The index is not queried
directly: that needs an authenticated URL, which makes the check
un-runnable at PR time and offline, and a gate that cannot run is not a
gate. The stated cost is that a publication whose tag step failed reads
here as unpublished — which is exactly the state
`recover-module-release.yml` exists to repair, so reporting it is correct.

dotmac-deployment-foundation.reason: FROZEN CANDIDATE, DELIBERATELY UNPUBLISHED AND DELIBERATELY UNMARKED. 0.3.0a2 was built ONCE as candidate artifact 9740182233 from source e930f878ce400b766b4a50feb0369021a28ab2fa (wheel sha256 2a6e0ccd040b05ab602be4b439e48dd61188b3b71ed6e80ecc8a482e70d57443, expires 2026-11-28). It is not tagged and not on any index, and the first authorization receipt, Lane 3 and both product cutovers bind to those exact bytes. NO DEVELOPMENT MARKER: the local-segment rule that applies to dotmac-kernel is scoped to PUBLISHED versions, and there is no published a2 artifact for this tree to misdescribe. Worse, VERSION lives inside the canonical descriptor, so `0.3.0a2+dev` moves the configuration digest off sha256:f481cfa2... and the rendered docker-compose.yml with it -- two of the five frozen components -- invalidating the candidate. Measured on 2026-08-31 and reverted; the rationale sits beside VERSION in version.py so it is not restored by reflex. Main's src/ may diverge from the candidate; that is recorded in docs/inventories/foundation-candidate-0.3.0a2.json, never by editing this version. Remove this row only when a2 is published or superseded by an authorized release.

dotmac-inbox-operations.reason: OUTSTANDING FOR SUB'S IDENTITY-PRESERVING ADOPTION AND THE ADR-0059 AVAILABILITY SLICE. Version a4 added typed historical presence, assignment, queue-entry and cursor imports; a5 adds the four-state availability owner, the browser heartbeat seam, the offline grace/requeue/supervisor-alert policy and the separated claim, cold-transfer, warm-transfer, requeue and escalation commands with their own declared permissions. Source presence is not registry evidence and Sub must not pin it until the protected release installs it back and tags the exact revision. Remove this row in the a5 release-record change, then repin Sub and retire its direct-model exception in the same adoption sequence; do not edit the declared version down.

dotmac-kernel.reason: DEVELOPMENT MARKER, DELIBERATELY UNPUBLISHABLE AND NOT A PENDING RELEASE. 0.1.0a99 IS published and tagged (dotmac-kernel-v0.1.0a99, peeled 8c92943062dbfe7f17bfa35264243709ec3d92c3). Main has since diverged from those bytes, so continuing to declare a bare 0.1.0a99 would have made the tree claim a version whose published artifact it no longer matches - structurally the defect that let dotmac-ui 0.1.0a7 reach the registry without map_frame. The local segment is a PEP 440 local version: no index accepts it, so it allocates nothing, cannot be published, and needs no release authorization. Michael authorizes release versions; nothing authorizes main to claim a version it is not. Remove this row by ALLOCATING the next version at release time, derived from immutable tags - never by editing the marker off to make this sweep quiet, which would restore the false claim. tests/architecture/test_declared_version_matches_published_tree.py enforces the invariant this row exists to keep true.

dotmac-runner-transport.reason: INTENDED UNTIL THE VMID 124 PILOT RETIRES THE LEGACY WRITER. The one-time local a1 wheel and bundle from 5d6381d were never published or tagged and are INVALIDATED: receipt acceptance did not bind adapter or provider-runner coordinates and accepted arbitrary well-formed evidence digests without the retained bytes. Reusing a1 for repaired bytes would make one version identify two contracts. a2 adds the typed provider-runner identity and canonical lifecycle-evidence documents, binds the adapter through the host specification, and re-hashes every retained document at acceptance. It remains absent from release-facilities.json. Remove this row only after one protected-main a2 bundle drives both repository diagnostics to terminal provider-recorded success, repeats after a cold reboot, and the observed-broker inventory plus its autonomous timer are retired with no_autonomous_return. The unchanged GitHub Actions adapter remains a1 and its >=0.1.0a1 dependency admits core a2. Foundation paths are outside this change.

dotmac-runner-transport-github-actions.reason: INTENDED UNTIL THE GITHUB ACTIONS PILOT PROVES THE EXACT SNAPSHOT. The adapter owns GitHub's current exact actions_inbound full-domain set, including its transitive result-storage names, but is deliberately absent from release-adapters.json until VMID 124 proves control, acquisition, result upload and provider-recorded success through the rendered proxy before and after a cold reboot. Metadata drift never auto-admits a domain. Remove this row only with the reviewed adapter-lane enrollment and pilot evidence; do not replace exact names with Azure CIDRs or a cloud-wide wildcard.
